statement: The function returns a result r. Let rows = r, define cnt(v) as the number of indices k with 0 <= k < len(nums) and nums[k] = v, and define maxcnt as the maximum of cnt(v) over all integers v with cnt(v) > 0. Then: (1) for every integer v, the number of pairs (i,j) with 0 <= i < len(rows), 0 <= j < len(rows[i]), and rows[i][j] = v is exactly cnt(v); (2) for every i with 0 <= i < len(rows), the entries of rows[i] are pairwise distinct, meaning rows[i][j] != rows[i][k] whenever 0 <= j < k < len(rows[i]); (3) len(rows) = maxcnt. Thus rows uses exactly the multiset of nums, every row has distinct integers, and the number of rows is minimal.
preconditions: len(nums) is an integer with 1 <= len(nums) <= 200, and for every index k with 0 <= k < len(nums), 1 <= nums[k] <= len(nums).
